waves.name: Wave 0

waves.name: Wave 2
waves.why: The storefront, its builder and the rules that drive it
waves.bn: দোকানের সামনের অংশ, পেজ সাজানোর টুল, কম্বো আর দোকানের নিয়ম।

waves.name: Wave 3
waves.why: The money path, end to end

waves.name: Wave 4
waves.why: Everything around an order once it exists
waves.bn: অর্ডার আসার পরের সব কাজ: জালিয়াতি ঠেকানো, কাস্টমার, প্যাকিং আর সাপোর্ট।

waves.name: Wave 5
waves.bn: খুঁজে পাওয়া আর প্রচার: SEO, ব্লগ, বিজ্ঞাপন আর সোশ্যাল মিডিয়া।

waves.name: Wave 6
waves.why: The control room and the numbers it governs
waves.bn: AI কন্ট্রোল রুম, হিসাব-রিপোর্ট আর সাইটের স্বাস্থ্য।

waves.name: Wave 7
waves.why: Imagery, once the catalogue is real

waves.name: Wave 8

waves.name: Wave 9

waves.name: Parked

bn.name: সার্ভারের ভিত্তি
bn.line: দোকান যে সার্ভারে চলবে, সেটা গুছিয়ে তৈরি করা — নিরাপত্তা, ডাটাবেস, ব্যাকআপ আর নজরদারি।

নিরাপত্তা, ডাটাবেস, ক্যাশ, HTTPS, রোজকার ব্যাকআপ আর সমস্যা হলে খবর — সব এখানে।
নতুন কোড এলে সাইট বন্ধ না করেই চালু হয়; সমস্যা হলে নিজে থেকে আগের ভার্সনে ফেরে।

changeNotes.title: owner: one README a developer can read in five years
changeNotes.text: (Filed as CN-011 because CN-010 is held by owner Note 53 in open GitHub PR #18.) (1) **README is the live, detailed front page** (`README.md`: status dashboard of all 28 stages, how it is built, local setup, the server, folder structure, features by area, PR log, change notes, docs map, notes for a future developer; `docs/README.md` indexes every docs file). After **every** merged PR the build agent updates the dashboard, adds the PR log row and updates the feature section of that area. (2) **Docs on the server:** every deploy copies the repo's `docs/` (with `README.md`, `BLUEPRINT.md`, `MASTER-REGISTER.md`) to the server, one way (repo → server), so the admin's "PR register" and "Blueprint & files" tabs (PR 594) always show the latest. (3) **Docs in backups:** every backup (PR 8 / 395 / 507; Azure Blob and Google Drive) carries a dated docs bundle — `README.md`, `docs/BLUEPRINT.md`, `docs/MASTER-REGISTER.md` and the whole `docs/` folder, with the commit hash — so a restore brings back the documentation of that exact version. (4) **Organisation standard, kept in every PR:** standard code style (lint and format checks), tests beside the code, clear names, a short header comment on each package saying what it is for, `docs/` kept current, and the blueprint and register changed only through CN notes. No new PR numbers: (1) is the S00 routine of PR 11, (2) lands on PR 4/17 (`deploy.yml`, `infra/deploy/deploy.sh`) and PR 594, (3) on PR 8, 395 and 507, (4) on PR 11 and 17.

changeNotes.title: owner: add the 8 best simulation ideas as optional settings; a Bengali guide per admin section
changeNotes.text: (1) Eight ideas from `docs/qa/SIMULATION-PLAN.md` §7 are added. Each is **off by default**, has its own on/off switch, and every number in it can be edited. Each lives in the admin section it belongs to; no new top-level menu. (a) **WhatsApp self-confirm** (idea 5): the reply 1/2/3 texts, the hours to wait before the call queue, and which orders it applies to. Section: Orders → Confirmation. Scope on PR 148, 292 and 545. (b) **Exact-amount line** (idea 10) on the sticker, SMS and tracking page, with the text and the report link. Section: Messages + Shipping labels. Scope on PR 179, 148 and 135. (c) **Packing proof photo** (idea 13): required or optional, and how many days to keep it. Section: Fulfilment. Scope on PR 182. (d) **RTO cost book** (idea 8): cost per RTO (courier charge, packaging, staff), by district, campaign, product, courier and reason. Section: Reports. Scope on PR 164, 192 and 267. (e) **One-trip size swap** (idea 17): the swap charge and the eligible areas. Section: Exchanges. Scope on PR 190. (f) **Day-1 WhatsApp care** (idea 15): the send hour, the text, and the Day-3 review request. Section: Messages. Scope on PR 295, 289 and 505. (g) **Eid order-by dates per district** (idea 19): the dates, the bands, the banner text, and pre-order with an advance amount. Section: Campaigns. Scope on PR 193 and 214. (h) **Gift mode** (idea 22): receiver name and phone, hide prices on the invoice, a gift note, and a "deliver on or after" date. Section: Checkout settings. This is the next free PR in S04. All 24 ideas stay listed in the plan, and the other 16 wait for the owner. (2) **Admin section guide (Bengali, a blueprint).** `docs/admin-guide/` holds one Bengali file per admin section (plain চলতি Bengali, Western digits) and an index. Each file says what the section is for, every menu and tab in it, what can be done there, every switch and number with its default, and what happens next. It is shown in the admin too, as a "এই সেকশনে কী করা যায়" help link on each section. **Every PR that adds or changes an admin screen updates its guide in the same PR** (same rule as README, CN-011). No other new PR numbers: (2) is the S00 routine of PR 11 plus PR 594's "Blueprint & files" tab.

changeNotes.title: owner: customer problems are found automatically, a "Running problems" list in the admin and at the top of README
changeNotes.text: (1) **Detect from real visits.** On every page and step of the journey (landing → product → bag → checkout → tracking → account), a small privacy-safe browser probe and server checks record: script errors, failed or slow requests, pages that fail to load, payment and API failures, stuck or repeated form errors (for example the phone field failing three times), "rage" clicks and dead clicks, checkout abandoned right after an error, slow loads by device and network type, and broken images. Each record carries the device, browser, network, area (district only) and journey step. **No name, phone, address or payment detail is ever recorded.** Visitor ids are random. (2) **Group and judge.** The backend groups records with the same cause into one **problem**, counts the visitors and orders it hit, estimates the lost sales, and marks it Urgent / Important / Can wait, with a plain Bengali summary of what went wrong, where and for whom. Short glitches that fixed themselves are kept too, under "short glitches". (3) **Status for each problem:** New · Fixing · Fixed (with how) · Could not fix (why) · Needs owner permission · Fixed, waiting for the owner's check before going live. (4) **Auto-fix:** when a fix touches no hard-rule item (money, prices, COD, blocking, deleting data) and needs no owner permission, the build agent fixes it through a normal PR (tests and gates, then merge), writes the note, and the problem moves to Fixed. Otherwise the problem goes to Needs owner permission. (5) **Where the owner sees it:** the admin **Site health → Customer problems** page (with the Server page, PR 423), which has a date view (today, yesterday, any day, trend) and a detail page for each problem; and the **top of README.md**, under "Running problems", with one line per open problem (date, short title, users hit, status) linking to `docs/problems/<id>.md` for details. Both are refreshed automatically by a scheduled workflow, with the problem data anonymised before it is written to GitHub. (6) **Sales link:** the weekly report says which problems most likely cost sales. No new PR numbers: it lands on S21 (PR 413–424, mainly PR 423 and the audit runner PR 570), PR 594 and the README routine (CN-011). Some parts are moved earlier: the probe and the problem list start as soon as the shop's checkout exists on new.extas.com.bd, so the simulation and staging tests feed it too.

changeNotes.title: owner: nothing reaches the owner broken
changeNotes.text: The owner found that after logging in, the admin on new.extas.com.bd showed "This page couldn't load". New gate: **after every deploy and every night**, a smoke test runs on the runner with Playwright against new.extas.com.bd. It signs in with a check account whose password lives only on the server, then visits every built storefront page and every built admin page, including the pages right after login. A page passes only when it loads, shows no error screen and no console error, and has no failed request. If any page fails, the deploy rolls back by itself and the fix comes before any new PR. Screenshots go to `docs/reports/smoke/latest/`, and the result is shown on the status page and in README. Every bug the owner finds gets a smoke check in the same fix PR. No new PR numbers: this lands on PR 4/17 (deploy) and Appendix C.

updates.text: **Updated 19 Oct 23:33 (owner server spec): Azure Blob is added** (supersedes "Drive only, no Blob"). **Blob:** continuous WAL archive for point-in-time restore to any minute; daily full backups; soft delete and versioning or immutability on, so a mistake or ransomware cannot wipe it; images and media in Blob with soft delete and versioning. **Google Drive stays mandatory:** the daily full encrypted copy, off-site with a different company; the second add-only Drive is a third copy. prs.title: NVMe temporary-disk boot unit — format and mount at every boot, folder layout, systemd ordering before services, admin NVMe card and …
prs.scope: **NVMe temporary-disk boot unit (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33).** On the E8ds_v6 the 440 GB local NVMe is **raw**: after a stop, deallocate, maintenance or move it comes up unformatted (Microsoft docs). A systemd unit runs at **every boot, before Redis, Postgres and Docker start**: detect the NVMe → format it ext4 if it is not already → mount at `/mnt/nvme` → create the folder layout (Redis working cache, image-processing intermediates, studio rendering, Postgres `temp_tablespaces`, build and pnpm caches, backup staging, session/queue scratch) → set ownership. Those services wait for the unit to succeed (systemd ordering). It holds temporary items only — **never** the database, code, uploads, final backups or kept logs. **Admin:** an NVMe card (mounted or not, free space, which services use it, PR 423); a Telegram alert if it is missing (PR 9). Pre-launch required.

prs.title: Hardware-aware auto profile and run-anywhere — limits from detected CPU and RAM, storage adapter (local / Blob / S3), CDN optional (owner …
prs.scope: **Hardware-aware auto profile and run-anywhere (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33).** Every RAM/CPU limit lives in **one config file, never in code**. On this box: PostgreSQL 16 GB / 2–3 CPU · Redis 6 GB / 1 CPU · Meilisearch 4 GB · Node/Next.js 16 GB / 4–6 CPU, 6 replicas · image/video worker 6 GB / 2 CPU · background jobs 4 GB / 1 CPU · Caddy 1 GB / 1 CPU · OS and the rest 11 GB, never squeezed = 64 GB. The profile **detects CPU and RAM and computes the limits itself** on any other machine (for example 4 vCPU / 16 GB) — no hand edits. **Run-anywhere:** a storage adapter (local disk / Azure Blob / S3-compatible) on the adapter framework of PR 18, so the shop works **without Blob**; it works **without the CDN** (images served from the server); handover-ready (S26). The admin shows each service's RAM and CPU against its limit (PR 423). Pre-launch required.

prs.scope: **Database performance pack (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33).** Built with the schema (PR 13). **Required indexes:** category page (category + store + in-stock + sort, one index); SKU and variant by colour and size; order by phone (runs on every order for the fraud engine); fuzzy name/address with **`pg_trgm`** (the fraud/duplicate engine, PR 519); customer order history; style hierarchy for profit (Polo → brand polo → solid polo, PR 536); order list filters (date, status, courier, store). **Slow query log** for anything over 100 ms, target under 50 ms for a normal query, and an admin **"slowest queries"** page (PR 423). **Reports** (profit, ads, dashboard charts) run on **materialized views** refreshed on a schedule, or on a low-priority report pool, so they never slow the shop. Site search stays on Meilisearch (PR 72). Pre-launch required — nothing deferred.

prs.title: Lumen theme layer, tokens and self-hosted fonts (CN-036; 6 Nov 2026)
prs.scope: **Lumen theme layer** (CN-036; S00; Lane A foundation; `docs/demo/admin-look/LUMEN-SPEC.md` §1). One central theme layer for the admin: every colour, radius, font and shadow is a CSS variable of the look (LUMEN-SPEC §1 light and dark tokens), nothing hardcoded in any admin page (the CI hardcode guard, PR 494, gains the admin rule). Light is the default mode; dark by the moon button, remembered per user on the account. The accent colour is a setting (Settings › Admin look › Colour; coral as shipped). Self-hosted fonts, no Google Fonts call: Bricolage Grotesque (display 700/800), Plus Jakarta Sans (body), Hind Siliguri (Bengali, already in the repo). Text on cards at least 14 px, headings at least 24 px on desktop. Motion (fade, count-up 700 ms, line draw, row slide-out, switch spring) honours `prefers-reduced-motion` and a per-user "Reduce motion" setting. A new look is a token set plus an optional shell variant, so PR 649–651 stay small. The CN-025 page designs A/B/C and ADMIN2-FRAMEWORK stay exactly as built.
prs.filedUnder: CN-036 additions — the admin look Lumen and two go-live items (6 Nov 2026)

prs.title: Import from ERP by style code — shop price as the buying price, B-grade listings, price-change flag, selling-price floor (CN-028; 25 Oct …
prs.scope: **Import from ERP by style code** (CN-028). The admin types a style code; every SKU of the style (colour, size, barcode, grade, `shopPrice`) comes in and groups into one product. The admin sees "bought from ERP at" (never shown to customers) and sets the selling price on top. A changed `shopPrice` updates the buying price and flags the admin; it never changes a selling price by itself. B-grade lines are separate listings (a switch, off by default). A **selling-price floor**: buying price + a minimum margin (a setting, empty until the owner sets it) blocks a price, coupon, combo or discount that falls below it. Launch.
prs.filedUnder: CN-028 additions — Retail and the ERP supplier model (25 Oct 2026)
prs.appendixTitle: Import from ERP by style code — shop price as the buying price, B-grade listings, price-change flag, selling-price floor (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)

status.note: import from the ERP by style code (CN-028, `erp.model` v6 only; no migration: the 0049 columns): `/admin/products/erp-import` (Products › more, `catalogue.import`) previews a style read with the store's own ERP key (CN-029 §16) and makes every SKU a draft grouped into one product (`COLOUR_MISSING` / `NOTHING_TO_IMPORT` refused; on the practice ERP it only previews); B grade as its own listing with `catalogue.bGrade.listing` (off) and the name suffix `catalogue.bGrade.nameSuffix` (registry v65). The ERP's shop price is the buying price (`shopPriceMinor`, never shown to customers), kept from the import, `variant.changed` and `shop-price.changed`; a change is flagged in "Buying prices that changed" (seen / all seen), never a change to a selling price. The selling-price floor (`catalogue.floor.minMarginPercent`, owner data, empty = off): a variant or combo set price below buying price + margin is refused (`BELOW_FLOOR`), the CSV preview shows it as an issue, and in the bag, checkout and product page every discount, coupon and set tier stops at the floor (`Quote.floorHeld`). Store A's import, prices and floor never touch store B (tests). qa-gate (30 Oct): a v5 store is refused (`ERP_V5`); at switch-over a style's SKUs already in one product without a style code adopt that product (shown in the preview), SKUs spread over other products (`SKU_IN_OTHER_PRODUCT`) or rows the catalogue cannot take (`ROW_NOT_ACCEPTED`) are listed and refused before any write, and sizes, products, variants, grades and buying prices are written in one transaction (a failure half-way leaves nothing); a re-import never turns a variant back on; a late, older `shop-price.changed` is ignored (`OLDER`) with the variant's row locked; the list length is `catalogue.shopPrice.changesShown`; **follow-ups (7 Nov, #93; follow-ups 521 part, 528, 529):** the rules simulator prices with the selling-price floor and says how often an offer stopped at it; "Buying prices that changed" names the fixed-price sets now below the floor; the offer editor says beforehand that a discount stops at the floor — display only, nothing changes a price; **follow-up (7 Nov, #96; follow-up 521, the order half):** the order keeps what its offers held back at the price floor (Order.floorHeldMinor, migration `0178_order_floor_held`) and the admin order page says "Offer stopped at the lowest price (held back)" with the amount; display only

prs.title: Site builder — the whole site dynamic (owner, 19 Oct 21:23: "like WordPress + Elementor, nothing fixed")
prs.scope: **Site builder — the whole site dynamic (owner, 19 Oct 21:23: "like WordPress + Elementor, nothing fixed").** From the backend, with preview before publish: **menus** (header nav / mega menu / phone menu / bottom bar — add, rename, reorder, hide, custom links, featured tile), **header** (announcement bar, icons on/off and order, logo), **footer** (columns, links, texts, contact block, social and payment marks), **categories and sub-categories** (create, rename, reorder, hide, image, intro, SEO), **product page blocks** (order and visibility of gallery, price row, colours, sizes, offers, buy-together, reviews, FAQ, care link), **content pages** (help, policies, about, careers, payment — rich text editor), **theme** (colours, fonts, spacing tokens with contrast check). Builds on PR 595 (home/category sections), 596 (side canvas) and 597 (launch default / snapshots / undo). Every change: draft → preview on phone/tablet/desktop → publish; per-device visibility; version history and undo. **Guardrails, not a blank canvas:** blocks snap to the responsive grid (no free pixel dragging that breaks phones), contrast and tap-size checks block bad publishes, checkout keeps its tested structure (texts, fields on/off and order editable; payment steps locked). Handover-ready: every default is data, a new owner configures everything here, the owner's own data never ships (PR 509).

prs.title: Four-layer cache plus invalidation — browser, Cloudflare, server page cache, Redis; purge rules; 15 s stock display with live checks at …
prs.scope: **Four-layer cache plus invalidation (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33).** **Browser** (images, CSS, JS, fonts for a long time, hashed file names) → **Cloudflare** (static files long; category and product pages for a few minutes, duration in settings; cart, checkout, account and admin never cached) → **server page cache** (built HTML for minutes, renewed the moment something changes) → **Redis** (settings, the Dhaka area list, products, categories, stock display). **Purge rules:** price change → that product, its category pages and the CDN; stock change → instantly; settings change → every place that setting is used; new product → category pages and the sitemap. **Stock:** the display cache lasts 15 s and every stock change event purges it at once; **add-to-bag and checkout always read live stock with a row lock (PR 198)** — nothing oversells. An admin **"Clear all cache"** button; cache hit %% on the Server page (PR 423). All durations are settings. Pre-launch required.
prs.filedUnder: S02 addition — four-layer cache (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33; CN-001)
prs.appendixTitle: Four-layer cache plus invalidation — browser, Cloudflare, server page cache, Redis; purge rules; 15 s stock display with live checks at bag and checkout; Clear all cache (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33)

status.note: the four-layer cache (new `@extas/cache`; registry v53 `registry-cache.ts`; no migration): the browser keeps hashed files a year; Cloudflare files, and category and product pages only with `cache.pages.cdn` (off); the server page cache for category and product pages (`cache.pages` {server on, cdn off, 5 / 5 minutes}); Redis carries the clear to every process; stock shown kept `cache.stockDisplaySeconds` 15 s while the bag and the checkout read live stock; `cache.tuning` {1000 pages, repeat 2 s, stats 7 days}. A price or stock change clears that product, its categories and Cloudflare at once; a setting clears every page; a new product its categories (and the sitemap tag); bag, checkout, account, admin and API never cached (proxy headers, Caddy `cache_headers`, `/api/internal/*` 404 from outside). Cloudflare purge adapter on its mock until the owner's token passes (Keys & connections); admin Settings › System › Cache (`/admin/settings/system/cache`, permission `system.cache`): the layers, hit counts, the times, "Clear all" with a confirmation and a reason (audited); the deploy clears the new app's cache (CACHE_HOOK_TOKEN, best effort); guide `cache.md`

The customer is never shown a score or a reason.

prs.title: Silent address backfill — a customer who writes only "Road 12, House 42" gets the Inside/Outside Dhaka question, unless his phone number is…
prs.scope: **Silent address backfill** — a customer who writes only "Road 12, House 42" gets the Inside/Outside Dhaka question, **unless his phone number is already known**. Then nothing is shown, nothing is prefilled, what he typed stays as he typed it, and the full address we hold is attached to the order in the backend for packing. A new address always wins over the stored one — he may have moved, or be sending a gift.

prs.title: Buy again — a past order's lines back in the bag at today's price and stock, sold-out sizes shown honestly, the normal checkout; off by …
prs.scope: **Buy again** (CN-034; S04; customer 360° finding 3, step `account/reorder`). "Buy again" on a past order's page and on its row in My orders puts the order's lines back in the bag: the same product, colour and size at **today's** price, offers and stock, never the old order's. A size that is sold out is shown as sold out with the sizes still in stock beside it, never swapped silently; a product no longer sold is named and left out; a set comes back as its set only while that set is still offered, otherwise as its separate pieces; add-ons, gifts and the old delivery charge are not copied. Nothing is ordered until the customer goes through the normal checkout, so the delivery charge, COD and every offer rule are the checkout's own. The new order carries a "bought again from #…" source tag that staff see on the order and reports can count. Setting `account.reorder` (**off by default**): the switch, the order states that offer it (delivered as shipped), whether the order list shows it too, and the button and notice words in English and Bengali. Section: the customer-account settings. Tests: a sold-out size, a product taken off sale, a changed price, a set no longer offered, the switch off.

prs.title: Orders to the ERP, v6 — line ids, whole-taka customer price split, erpTotal and billedAt, hold and short-stock handling, the …
prs.scope: **Orders to the ERP, v6** (CN-028; extends PR 199 and 200). `lineId`, `customerPrice` in whole taka (the remainder of a combo or discount split on the last piece), `deliveryCharge`, `advancePaid`, `grade`; the answer's `erpTotal`, `shopPrice` per line and `billedAt` are stored. `409 ACCOUNT_ON_HOLD` queues the order and **pauses checkout by itself** (`erp.hold.pauseCheckout`, on) until `account.released`; `409 NO_SHOP_PRICE` stops that SKU; `409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK` retries with a **new** idempotency key. A line filled from Return stock shows "From ERP return stock"; if that piece fails the packing check (`order.line.short`) the order waits and the admin chooses wait, replace or cancel the line. Launch.
prs.filedUnder: CN-028 additions — Retail and the ERP supplier model (25 Oct 2026)
prs.appendixTitle: Orders to the ERP, v6 — line ids, whole-taka customer price split, erpTotal and billedAt, hold and short-stock handling, the packing-check short line (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)

status.note: orders to the ERP v6 (v6 stores only; v5 unchanged): one `lineId` per piece with quantity 1 (follow-up 491), `customerPrice` in whole taka (the order's discount spread by value, a combo's remainder on its last piece: 1600 over 3 → 533, 533, 534), `deliveryCharge`, `advancePaid` (online + wallet), `grade`; ErpOrder / ErpOrderLine rows kept with the order (line ids stable across revisions); the answer's `erpTotal`, each line's `shopPrice` and `fromReturnStock` stored. A 409 the ERP keeps against its key is HELD with its reason and goes again by itself with a new key round (migration `0053_erp_orders_v6`: `ErpPush.keyRound`, `heldReason`): `ACCOUNT_ON_HOLD` pauses checkout (`erp.hold.pauseCheckout`, on; `PAUSED`, the bag kept) until `account.released` or the account check; `INSUFFICIENT_STOCK` when the ERP has the stock; `NO_SHOP_PRICE` stops that SKU (`shopPriceMissingAt`) until the ERP takes it; an order cancelled before the ERP had it is never sent. `order.line.short` / `filled` handled; the order page's ERP card shows "From ERP return stock" and the admin decides a short line (WAIT, REPLACE, CANCEL; `orders.lines`, audited). Follow-up 490: the order check (`inventory.erp.checkOrders`, every `erp.account.checkMinutes`) reads the account and the ERP's own copy of open orders, so a lost line webhook or answer is caught up. Registry v66 (`erp.orders.*`). Store isolation tested. 31 Oct (CN-033, built, CN-031 lane A; not counted again): `erp.orders.bGradeOpen` (v72, off): while off a B-grade piece is not sold on a v6 store, no B-grade REPLACE is asked for, and a `422` naming `bGradeSkus` holds the order as `B_GRADE_CLOSED` with an admin message (woken once when the switch goes on); the practice ERP answers the same 422; the acceptance check sends a B-grade line only while open; **follow-ups (7 Nov, #93; follow-ups 532, 539 part b):** `shop-price.changed` lets the SKU sell again and sends the orders held for its price at once; orders the ERP keeps refusing raise one alert after the owner's hours (registry v239 `erp.orders.heldAlertAfterHours`, empty = off); **follow-up (7 Nov, #96; follow-up 534):** ErpOrder.orderId → Order and ErpOrderLine.orderItemId → OrderItem are foreign keys (migration `0177_erp_order_foreign_keys`, added NOT VALID, validated when every old row names a real order or line)

prs.title: Band mapping — one band per area, simple
prs.scope: **Band mapping** — one band per area, simple. **Dhaka City = the official DNCC + DSCC map**, nothing else. Sub-area = the owner's list, which is the only exception to the map. Everywhere else is one flat rate. The charge the customer sees is a figure the owner fixes in the admin — it does not depend on which courier the parcel ends up on. The sub-area band has three settings: its own charge · folded into Dhaka City · folded into the outside-Dhaka flat charge.

prs.title: Ambiguity resolver — reads the whole line, and waits
prs.scope: **Ambiguity resolver — reads the whole line, and waits.** Nothing is decided while the cursor is still in the address field: people write the district a few words later ("Gabtoli Bus Stand, **Dhaka**"; "Masterpara, Gabtali, **Bogura**"). On blur, or a long enough pause, the resolver reads the complete address — a district, parent area or postcode anywhere in it settles the band **silently, with no question**. A postcode settles it (1216 Dhaka, 5820 Bogura); a co-occurring local name narrows it; a returning customer's saved address outranks any guess. **Only a line still ambiguous after that full read asks**, and once the customer confirms, nothing silently changes it.
prs.filedUnder: S06 additions — the delivery-zone engine (§60, 18 Oct)
prs.appendixTitle: Ambiguity resolver — reads the whole line, and waits

status.note: ambiguity resolver: reads the whole line after `delivery.resolver.settleMs` (900 ms) or blur, asks "Where is this address?" only when still ambiguous; admin Try-an-address; resolve APIs

prs.title: Phone-entry risk check — our database and the courier fraud checks queried in the background while the customer keeps typing
prs.scope: **Phone-entry risk check** — our database and the courier fraud checks queried **in the background while the customer keeps typing**. Never blocks the form; a slow or failed check **passes the customer**. It catches a pattern, not a slip: 20 orders with 5–8 cancelled is not a flag; five parcels from several couriers all cancelled is. Recency weighted.
prs.filedUnder: S06 additions — the delivery-zone engine (§60, 18 Oct)
prs.appendixTitle: Phone-entry risk check — our database and the courier fraud checks queried in the background while the customer keeps typing

status.note: phone-entry risk check and the "pattern, not a slip" signal (After launch, batch 5; settings `checkout.phoneRisk` and `risk.signals.pattern`, v109, both off): a whole typed number pings `/api/checkout/phone-risk` once (the answer is always `{ok: true}`, the form never waits); the server asks every connected courier fraud source within a time budget, keeps each answer for `cacheHours` (`CourierFraudCheck`), rate limited per IP; the pattern is the recency-weighted share of failed parcels over his own orders, the same device, the same person and each courier's answer; the checkout's risk look carries the device, name and address (SIM-F-015); two Risk rules cards; the order page explains the pattern

status.note: a defect or missing piece at packing (answers 41, 42; SIM-F-006): "Report defect / out of stock" on a line opens a packing card (DAMAGED / NOT_FOUND; the stock sync's SHORTAGE card shows the same way), and with `fulfilment.packing.issues` (v59: hold on, reasons defective-item / waiting-stock, 48 hours to decide, edit reason customer-asked) the order is held with it, from confirmed or from picking (the order machine now holds from PROCESSING and releases back to it); any open card stops packing and booking; a person decides each card through the order service — found / fine (a shortage card needs `inventory.audit`), another size or colour at the same price (`orders.edit`), send the rest (`orders.edit`; a paid order gets a REQUESTED refund, PR 172's flow), cancel as out of stock (`orders.cancel`) — and "Call the customer" leaves one PACKING_ISSUE call task; never cancelled or refunded by itself, a card past the hours only marked late; the last decided card releases the hold; a booked parcel is not edited (BOOKED); `POST /api/admin/packing/orders/{id}/issue`, `…/issues/{issueId}/resolve`, `…/call` (`fulfilment.pack`); **follow-ups (7 Nov, #96; follow-ups 469 order page, 468 Needs you now):** an open packing card shows on the order page with its pieces and the way to the packing screen; open packing cards and late ones are "Needs you now" lines on the Dashboard and in the To do drawer

prs.scope: **Charge mismatch log** — when the courier resolves a different real location than the band the customer was charged for, **nothing is changed and nobody is messaged**. prs.title: Courier return lists to the ERP — scan at hand-back, counted pieces and condition note, early courier claim (replaces the shop-side …
prs.scope: **Courier return lists to the ERP** (CN-028; replaces the quality check of PR 187 and ORD-05a). Staff scan the consignments at hand-back, count the pieces and write a short condition note (a photo of the sealed bag when `returns.handback.photo` is on); the list goes by `POST /return-lists` with `receivedCount` and `note`. A count that differs from the ERP's expectation starts the courier claim at once. Returns that do not come through a courier (a showroom) use `courier: HAND`. The shop never decides whether a piece can be sold again; the owner decides in the ERP. Launch.

prs.title: Exchange through the ERP — line marking, price-difference consent, stock-first rule, the 4-day return watch, late-return mark (CN-028; 25 …
prs.scope: **Exchange through the ERP** (CN-028; extends PR 185–190). Within 72 hours of the courier's "delivered" the admin approves and **marks the lines** exchanged. Before approving: live ERP stock of the new piece, regular orders first (an exchange waits and the admin is told), and the price difference shown; if the new price is higher the customer pays the difference (`exchange.passPriceRiseToCustomer`, on; the exchange terms are updated). The exchange goes as a new order naming the old order and line, with a clear note. The shop shows the 4-day watch, the risk list from `GET /exchanges?status=pending`, and a **late-return mark** (`POST /exchanges/{id}/late-return`). The customer's original sale stands; the swap difference and exchange charge are Retail's income lines. Launch.

prs.scope: **Blog as a complete, standard section of the shop, with our own ad placements (owner, 19 Oct 12:20).** Blog features: categories (pillars) and sub-categories, tags, author/reviewer pages, search, archive, featured and related posts, reading time, contents, share, RSS, newsletter sign-up, Bengali twins. **House ads only (no outside ad networks):** slots on the blog home (top banner, between cards), category pages, inside the article (after paragraph N, AdSense-style), sidebar on desktop, end of article, and an optional popup per post. status.note: the customer model, the merge rules and the single view by phone (new package `@extas/customers`; migration `0047_customer_merge` additive: `Customer.mergedIntoId` / `mergedAt` with an index, `CustomerMerge` with `MERGED` / `NOT_SAME`, the rules that matched, the note, who, the Idempotency-Key and the undo; registry v60 `registry-customers.ts`): a merge only points the joining profile at the one that stays (one level, nothing moves, nothing is deleted), refused when either is erased, archived, already merged or has merged profiles of its own; "not the same person" keeps a pair from being suggested again; a split (or a "not the same" taken back) needs a note and is audited. Suggestions from `customers.merge` {suggest on, signals e-mail · WhatsApp number is the other's phone · name + address · the same identity on an order (all on), 20 a page, note required off}. The single view by phone: every profile and every number of the person, order counts and lifetime value from `@extas/metrics` (`customerKpis`: Sales = delivered only beside Ordered value, CN-022; refusals without the shop's own mistakes), any written form of a number finds him (`customerByPhone`). Phone masked without `customers.phone` (`customers.phoneMask` {first 3, last 3}); every open and every copy or call written to "Who looked at this customer" first (Note 24.1). Permissions `customers.read`, `customers.phone`, `customers.merge`. Customers → To review (`/admin/customers/review`, demo V12.4 CUS-05): the "Same person?" pairs side by side, Merge / Not the same person, the decisions with Split; API under `/api/admin/customers`; **follow-up (7 Nov, #94; follow-up 478):** the sample seed gives the sample customer a "Same person?" pair and a merged profile, so the smoke test and the device gate see both; **follow-up (7 Nov, #96; follow-up 471):** Customer settings gets cards for the merge rules, the phone mask, the customer list and one customer's page

status.note: Multi-provider adapter: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, all dynamic (C1.5; no migration — `AiProvider`/`AiModel` and `AI_PROVIDER` already in the full S00 schema; `packages/adapters/src/ai-writer/`): the AI writer's practice-only adapter (PR 221/293/243) gets its first four live providers — one key + one model id each (the owner types the model id his key may use; no model name trusted as current, per the blueprint), each a row in Keys & connections (`exclusive: false`, several may be on at once, like the payment gateways). Every provider answers the exact same `AiWriter` contract through one shared prompt-and-parse layer (`prompts.ts`, `live.ts`) — "write only from the facts given, reply as one JSON object" — so a draft from Claude, GPT, Gemini or an OpenRouter model is read the same way; a model that answers with anything else is a clean `AdapterError`, never a guess. OpenAI and OpenRouter share one Chat-Completions-shaped completer (`openai-compatible.ts`); OpenRouter's two attribution headers are optional. Falls back to the practice writer until a connection's key and model are in and its Test (one real sample SEO draft) passes. Free / OpenRouter-style models stay a hard no in production until PR 580's qualification; per-agent/per-job model choice is PR 307. Keys & connections guide updated with the four new rows.

prs.title: Per-agent monthly spend cap
prs.scope: **Per-agent monthly spend cap**, with the 80% warning and the 100% pause
prs.appendixTitle: Per-agent monthly spend cap

status.note: Per-agent monthly spend cap, with the 80% warning and the 100% pause (C1.6; no migration — `AiAgent.monthlyCapMinor` already in the full S00 schema, additive, unused until now; permission `ai.control`): each agent card in AI › Control room gets its own monthly spend cap (`CapInput`, new `apps/web/src/lib/admin-ai/spend-cap.ts`) — a plain amount in the store's own currency, major units, empty is "no cap" (off, the default). `POST /api/admin/ai {key, monthlyCapMinor}` validates the value (422 `INVALID_CAP` for anything but `null` or a whole number 1..2,147,483,647), audits `ai.agent.cap`, idempotent. `agentCapState` (none/ok/warned/paused, whole-number cross-multiplication so the 80% line is exact, never a float) and `wouldExceedCap` are built as pure, tested enforcement primitives ready for the job dispatcher to call before paying for one more run — no such dispatcher exists yet, since nothing in the codebase writes an `AiUsageLedger` row outside a test fixture (PR 306/307/308 are equally honest about this). What is real and live, not speculative: `checkAgentCapAlerts`, run on every read of the Control room, which sends the owner's Telegram warning the moment any agent's spend crosses 80%/100% of its own cap — deduplicated through the audit log (`ai.agent.capWarn80`/`ai.agent.capPaused`, once per crossing per month), never throwing (a Telegram hiccup never breaks the screen). The owner reads only চলতি বাংলা (CLAUDE.md), so the alert text is always Bengali, independent of whichever language an English-reading staff member has the admin UI itself set to; at 100% new generations would pause (already-approved output stays live, the shop unaffected) — the worked example the Blueprint gives for the Photoshoot agent, now true "as with any agent", the same widening PR 305 did for keep-on. status.note: The masking layer applied before anything leaves the server (A5.1–A5.4, FAQ 55; no migration, no owner setting, no admin page — a transport-level safety net, not a screen): new `packages/adapters/src/ai-writer/masking.ts` — `maskPersonalData` is a pattern-based safety net that strips every e-mail address and Bangladeshi-shaped phone number (however punctuated or prefixed: bare, `+880`, `880`, or the full `00880` international dial) out of a piece of text, replacing each with a plain `[EMAIL]`/`[PHONE]` token; `maskKnownIdentity` is exact-value stripping for a future job that already holds a real customer record (name/phone/e-mail/address), case-insensitive, three-character minimum so a stray initial is left alone. `liveAiWriter` (live.ts) now wraps every provider's `Completer` so `system`/`user` are masked right before the one call in the package that actually leaves the server over HTTP — a safety net layered on top of whatever provider-routing policy the data carries, never a replacement for one. Today's three draft kinds (SEO, campaign, article) carry no real customer content, so this is built ahead of the S14/S22 jobs that will send one (support replies, rider notes) — the same honestly-inert-until-wired shape earlier S15 PRs shipped before any AI key existed; `maskKnownIdentity` is exported and fully tested but not yet called by any job. No admin page changes.

prs.scope: **Model auto-suggest with free-model qualification** — for every agent job the system suggests a model with its reason; the owner accepts or changes it. prs.title: Chief agent — জ্ঞানী Gyani as virtual CEO (প্রধান এজেন্ট), chain of command
prs.scope: **Chief agent — জ্ঞানী Gyani as virtual CEO (প্রধান এজেন্ট), chain of command.** The owner charges one agent; Gyani answers to him and charges the other six by their performance. Asked "why are sales down this month / this week?", "why was today's courier entry wrong?", "why is this bug on the category page?", Gyani investigates across every section (orders, ads, stock, delivery, site errors, the agents' work logs), names **which agent's area caused it, with evidence**, assigns the fix to that agent, tracks it to done and reports back. Broad knowledge beyond its own stages (business, finance, operations, marketing, tech) — curriculum adds an executive/general-management track. Second only to the owner. **Free to do:** research, reports, analysis, assigning and reviewing work, warnings to agents (written into their appraisals PR 578). **Only with the owner's approval:** any money movement or refund, any COD amount change on an order, price or discount changes, ad budget increases, blocking anyone, deleting data, anything that cannot be undone. The permission list is a dashboard setting the owner edits; enforced by code. Lives in S15 AI 360 (org chart, open investigations, who-owns-what).

prs.title: Telegram identity and command routing
prs.scope: **Telegram identity and command routing.** All agents share the owner's one Telegram bot. Every message starts with the sender's identity — photo/emoji, name, Bengali name, **employee code**, role (e.g. "🏹 Tirondaj তীরন্দাজ · A360-07 · Ads") — so the owner always knows who sent it. When the owner writes a command naming an agent or its code ("A360-07 budget report", "@Bhandari courier entry check"), the task is **assigned to that agent automatically**, appears on its profile as an assignment, and the agent replies in the same thread when done. No name → goes to the chief (Gyani), who routes it. Approvals come back as buttons (Approve / Reject / Ask why). Also visible in the dashboard.

prs.title: Continuous learning engine — Tirondaj (ads) and Doot (SEO/marketing) are the two power agents
prs.scope: **Continuous learning engine — Tirondaj (ads) and Doot (SEO/marketing) are the two power agents.** They learn without stopping from: official docs (Meta, Google, TikTok, Search Central), the big practitioner blogs on SEO and paid ads, Reddit communities (PPC, Facebook ads, SEO, e-commerce), YouTube tutorials incl. South-Asian e-commerce channels (read through transcripts), LinkedIn and Facebook posts of known specialists (where readable; through a paid tool if needed), case studies. **When stuck:** research all sources → solve → the solution becomes a skill in its basket. **Quality gate (no shortcut learning):** a tip becomes a skill only after it is checked against the official docs or two independent good sources, tested in a sandbox or small live test, and written with its source, date and confidence; tips that fail are recorded as "doesn't work for us". **Practice tasks with deadlines** (e.g. get a new page indexed within 3 days, a long-tail keyword into Google's top 10, a test campaign under the CPA cap) graded in their appraisals. **Paid data tools** (e.g. an SEO suite) proposed with cost and reason — the owner approves and pays.

prs.title: Retail's ERP account ledger and the pipeline stock — append-only entries, payments to the ERP, opening balance (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)
prs.scope: **Retail's ERP account ledger and the pipeline stock** (CN-028). An append-only list of entries (bill, exchange extra / adjustment / bill / credit, return credit, payment, switch transfer, reversal, adjustment) with the ERP event id (unique forever), the ERP's own date, whole-taka signed amount and a hash chain; the balance owed; the pipeline stock at buying price from the shop's own piece states; `waitingCheck` and `exchangesAtRisk` beside it. Payments to the ERP are recorded by the Accounts role or the owner and matched to the ERP's `payment.recorded`. Opening balance at the switch. Launch.
prs.filedUnder: CN-028 additions — Retail and the ERP supplier model (25 Oct 2026)
prs.appendixTitle: Retail's ERP account ledger and the pipeline stock — append-only entries, payments to the ERP, opening balance (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)

prs.title: Books match engine — daily, weekly, monthly, yearly and lifetime match with the ERP, differences, month-close gate, explain view (CN-028; …
prs.scope: **Books match engine** (CN-028; the heart of `docs/RETAIL-ERP-MODEL.md` §3.4 and §4). Checks A–F every night at 01:30 (account and statement rows, the profit-and-loss tie formula, returns and exchanges, stored daily summaries, fixed costs, billed orders); an immutable day close; week, month, year and lifetime built from the day closes and checked against each other and the ERP's balance; zero tolerance; timing waits only while the pull fetches a known event; differences listed by class and fixed only by reversing and adding (`books.adjust`, PIN, reason, the ERP's matching entry); a month closes only when every day matched (an override needs the PIN and is logged); the Books status card and the "Needs you now" rows; the **explain this number** view on every figure. Launch.
prs.filedUnder: CN-028 additions — Retail and the ERP supplier model (25 Oct 2026)
prs.appendixTitle: Books match engine — daily, weekly, monthly, yearly and lifetime match with the ERP, differences, month-close gate, explain view (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)

status.note: The books match engine: checks A–F per store link with zero tolerance (account rows by group, the tie formula, returns, the stored summary, fixed costs, billed orders), job `inventory.books.close` once a night after `books.close.runAt` (looked for every `books.close.checkMinutes`, `books.recheck.days` closed days again), an append-only hash-chained day close per day (a new version when it moves, HISTORY_CHANGED for a matched day), weeks and the lifetime check from the day closes, the month close only when every day matched (`books.close.requireMatched`) or with the owner's override (PIN, reason, kept), re-open as a new version, the year sign-off; a difference fixed only by a reversal plus a new entry (`books.adjust`, the owner's PIN, a reason, the ERP's matching row; PRIOR_PERIOD in a closed month); the owner's books PIN (scrypt hash only, never logged, lock after `books.pin.maxAttempts`); Money → Books → Match, Differences, Closes and the Needs-you-now row; migration `0055_books_pin`; registry v68; CN-029 Phase 1 (Gyani);

tests: follow-up 559 c):** the year sign-off and the re-opened month end to end on PostgreSQL — a re-opened month whose late paisa was put right in a later month closes again as a new version with the owner's reason, the other months close without an override, a year with a month still open is refused naming every open month, and once every month is closed the year is signed off once (test only)

prs.title: Daily summary to the ERP — 00:30 send, retry queue, summary.missing, gap fill, re-send window, categories not yet known, log (CN-028; 25 …
prs.scope: **Daily summary to the ERP** (CN-028). Builds the day from the shop's own records (delivery-day basis, the exact source of every line in `docs/RETAIL-ERP-MODEL.md` §3.3), sends it at 00:30, retries with backoff until accepted, answers `summary.missing` at once, fills gaps by `GET /daily-summaries?from&to`, re-sends an open day when a late fact changes it (`books.resend.days`), lists unknown categories in `incomplete` (never 0), keeps every summary it sent and the ERP's reply in a log the admin sees, and checks the ERP's stored copy against its own. Launch.
prs.filedUnder: CN-028 additions — Retail and the ERP supplier model (25 Oct 2026)
prs.appendixTitle: Daily summary to the ERP — 00:30 send, retry queue, summary.missing, gap fill, re-send window, categories not yet known, log (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)

status.note: daily summary to the ERP (CN-029 Phase 1): each shop day from the shop's own records on the delivery-day basis, every line from its one source (§3.3), unknown lines in `incomplete`, the exact minor lines kept beside the whole-taka body (`minorLines`, migration 0056; PR 616's tie reads them); append-only versions, sent at `erp.summary.sendAt` and retried until accepted (a 4xx refusal waits for a person), a late fact re-sent within `books.resend.days` (never a closed month), `summary.missing` answered at once, the hourly check against the ERP's stored copy; per store and per link, v5 builds nothing; the Books status card and **Money → Daily summary** (`/admin/money/books/daily`); registry v69; **follow-ups (7 Nov, #93; follow-ups 566, 568):** a day on the Daily summary page opens that day's lines with their sources (the match page's day explain); on the practice ERP without its data a day says "Waiting for the ERP key"; **follow-up (7 Nov, #94; follow-up 569):** the nightly smoke checks that no daily summary or month waited for the ERP more than a day, and "not run yet" only before the first match run; **follow-up (7 Nov, #96; follow-up 563, parts b and c):** the daily summary's pieces handed back are net of a piece put back with the courier the same day, and a test holds that a later courier result moves the delivery charge to its own day; part a stays open (a design decision)

prs.title: Fixed costs and the extra cost lines — salary, rent, utilities, accessories, payment fees (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)
prs.scope: **Fixed costs and the extra cost lines** (CN-028). A Retail dashboard page where the owner sets the monthly fixed costs (salary, rent, utilities, other) and raises them when they rise; sent by `PUT /fixed-costs/{month}` and shown with the same by-day spreading rule as the ERP (exact to the paisa, the remainder on the last day). New cost lines for accessories and payment-gateway or COD fees feed the daily summary. Fixed costs never go into the daily `costs.other`. Launch.
prs.filedUnder: CN-028 additions — Retail and the ERP supplier model (25 Oct 2026)
prs.appendixTitle: Fixed costs and the extra cost lines — salary, rent, utilities, accessories, payment fees (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)

status.note: fixed costs and the extra cost lines (CN-029 Phase 1): **Money → Costs** (`/admin/money/costs`, `fixedcosts.write`): a month's salary, rent, utilities and other, empty as shipped, each change an append-only version sent by `PUT /fixed-costs/{month}` and checked against `GET /fixed-costs`, shown by day with the ERP's spread (exact to the paisa, remainder on the last day), never in `costs.other`; daily cost lines (packaging, accessories, payment and COD fees, courier, ads, other) for today or an open day, reversed by a negative entry, the day re-sent; capped by `books.costs.maxLineMinor` / `maxMonthMinor`; **follow-up (7 Nov, #94; follow-up 567):** the daily cost lines get their own permission (`costlines.write`), so staff can enter packaging without setting salaries; **follow-up (7 Nov, #96; follow-up 565):** an imported courier COD statement or gateway statement writes its charges or fees as one cost entry on the DELIVERY or PAYMENT_FEES line (`books.costs.fromStatements`, registry v274, both off; record only, never failing the import); the "Costs from statements" card on Money › Costs

prs.scope: **Signed calls from the ERP to the shop** (CN-028). `GET /erp-api/top-products` and `GET /erp-api/customers`, signed like the webhooks (`X-Extas-Signature` over `METHOD\nPATH?QUERY\nTIMESTAMP`, constant-time check, refused when older than 5 minutes), opened on the staging password gate for that path only, every call logged, customer data returned live and never pushed. The admin shows the base URL to put into the ERP. After launch.
prs.filedUnder: CN-028 additions — Retail and the ERP supplier model (25 Oct 2026)
prs.appendixTitle: Signed calls from the ERP to the shop — top products and customers on click (CN-028; 25 Oct 2026)

status.note: signed calls from the ERP to the shop (CN-028, docs/erp/site-changes-v6.md §2.7; no migration): `GET /erp-api/top-products?from&to&limit` (Sales by SKU from `@extas/metrics` `salesBySku`: pieces, net sales, profit over the cost snapshot) and `GET /erp-api/customers?page&pageSize&search` (`@extas/customers` `erpCustomerPage`: one row per person who ordered, total spent = Sales), answered live and never pushed. Signed `X-Extas-Signature` over `METHOD\nPATH?QUERY\nTIMESTAMP`, constant-time, refused beyond `erp.siteApi.maxAgeSeconds` (300); the store is the one whose own secret verifies (CN-029 §16: the new optional third ERP key `signingSecret`, else the webhook secret; v6 stores only; a shared secret refused). Today the key and the card are the mother store's, on Keys & connections; each store's own key and card come with its ERP link page (PR 619). Off per store (`erp.siteApi.enabled`, registry v65) until switched on on the new "The ERP asks the shop" card on `/admin/integrations` (`vault.write`), which shows the base URL, the latest verified calls and the refused calls summed. qa-gate (30 Oct): a call refused from the request alone (path, method, no or a malformed signature) reads no database, setting or vault; refusals are only counted (one SecurityEvent `erp.site-call.refused` summary per `erp.siteApi.refusedLogMinutes`), after `erp.siteApi.refusedPerMinute` refused calls a minute further unverified calls get 429 without a store lookup, and only a verified caller's call gets its own `erp.site-call` row (no customer data); the search length is `erp.siteApi.searchMaxChars`; the query is signed percent-encoded. The preview gate lets only these two GET paths through, matched on the raw request target case for case, as are the ERP and WhatsApp webhook exemptions (gate v5; CI runs the live gate checks on a pinned Caddy 2.10.2). After launch; **follow-up (7 Nov, #93; follow-up 526):** the ERP's signed calls can refuse a signature already answered (registry v238 `erp.siteApi.refuseReplays`, off; code REPLAYED)

tests: CI runs the live gate checks on a pinned Caddy 2.10.2)

prs.title: The customer's own privacy request — a copy of his data or its erasure, asked from his account, filed into PR 382's staff screen; staff …
prs.scope: **The customer's own privacy request** (CN-034; S18; customer 360° finding 6, step `account/privacy-request`; feeds PR 382). On his account's profile a signed-in customer asks for **a copy of his data** or for **its erasure**, with an optional note, after a plain notice of what erasure keeps (orders keep money, lines and history without his contact details; the shop's legal, money and stock records stay). The request goes into PR 382's staff list on Settings › Privacy & data as a request from the customer himself, with who, when and his account; the account page shows it as received and then its outcome. **Nothing is erased by the request**: staff approval and PR 382's way of carrying it out stay exactly as built (owner only, the typed word, never while an order is on its way); a copy of the data is prepared only after staff approve it and is given through his signed-in account. One open request per kind per customer; the same tap twice is one request. Setting `privacy.customerRequests` (**off by default**; it shows only while PR 382's `privacy.erasureRequests` is on): the switch, which kinds are offered, and the notice and button words in English and Bengali. Audited. Tests: the request files and changes nothing, a second tap, the switch off, a guest cannot ask for someone else.

prs.appendixTitle: Support core: conversation/message model, threads, attachments, internal notes, assignment, who-replied log (V1 B4.14 item 1) (derived)

status.note: the support core (new package `@extas/support`; migration `0050_invoice_support` additive: Conversation subject, order, last direction and preview, waiting since, assigned at; Message sender name, request key, fail reason, unique per external id and per press; MessageAttachment file name, type, size, source; `ConversationEvent` the who-did-what log, append-only at the database; settings registry v63 `registry-support.ts`, group `support`): one conversation per person per channel with its messages in order — the customer's, the shop's replies with the sender's name kept as it was, internal notes the customer never sees — and their files (image, video, PDF, checked by their contents, kept in our storage); OPEN / WAITING / SOLVED, a solved one reopens when the customer writes; take, let go, give to someone who may reply; a reply sent twice is one message, a stale screen is refused (`STALE`). Channels plug in later (PR 426): a channel kind and an adapter (`SupportChannelAdapter`), inbound through `receiveMessage`; with none connected a reply is kept as NOT_SENT (`CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`). Support → Inbox (`/admin/support`: views open, waiting, mine, not taken, solved, all; search; channel), one conversation (`/admin/support/c/[id]`: thread, reply / note box with files, status, owner, customer and order, the log) and Support settings (`/admin/support/settings`): `support.inbox` (50 a page, 2000 characters, take on reply off, waiting after a reply on), `support.attachments` under More options (on, 4 a message, 10 MB, image / video / PDF); a customer's number is masked by `customers.phoneMask` (PR 284), whole only with `customers.phone`. Permissions `support.read`, `support.reply`, `support.assign`, `support.settings`. The sample seed gains a sample live-chat channel with three conversations

prs.scope: **Messenger button on the shop** (CN-034; S22; customer 360° finding 7, step `support/messenger-button`). A Messenger chat link or button beside the shop's other support channels — the header WhatsApp icon, the site chat (PR 426) and the contact page — that opens the store's own Facebook Page in Messenger (`m.me/<page>`), with an optional "ref" naming the page and product it was tapped on so the chat starts with context. The Page address is the store's own setting (owner data, empty as shipped), never code; the button shows only while it is set. Setting `support.messengerButton` (**off by default**): the switch, the Page address, where it shows (header, product page, help and contact pages, the order page), the label and the hint words in English and Bengali. Each tap is counted with the other support-channel clicks. Tests: off and empty show nothing, the link is built from the setting, the device gate on the pages it shows on.

prs.title: Content calendar, approval queue, auto-schedule rules, per-platform limits (V1 C5.5)
prs.appendixTitle: Content calendar, approval queue, auto-schedule rules, per-platform limits (V1 C5.5) (derived)

status.note: content calendar, approval queue, auto-schedule rules, per-platform limits (Blueprint C5.3, C5.5 point 4; `packages/studio/src/schedule.ts`, the `SocialScheduleRule` table S00's skeleton already carries, no migration): `SocialScheduleRule` CRUD (add/edit/switch/archive-restore, `studio.write`, never deleted) — a cadence (posts+reels a day), active weekdays and categories, optionally pinned to one account; `nextActiveDayOf` is a pure "next active day" preview only — honest scope unchanged from PR 307/308 (S15): the actual dispatcher that would pick products/templates and fire a render+post on schedule needs both the real compositor (PR 439's own gap) and a `packages/jobs` cron slot not wired for this stage, so it is not built rather than faked. What PR 442 does enforce for real: the **approval queue** (`decideSocialPost`, `studio.approve` — approve moves a `PENDING_APPROVAL` post to `SCHEDULED`/`PUBLISHING` exactly where it would have landed had the account already run free; reject is final, kept for the record); **reschedule** (`rescheduleSocialPost`, `studio.generate`) moves a not-yet-sent post to a new time or clears it; the **calendar** (`studioCalendar`, `studio.read`) groups every post with a `scheduledAt`/`publishedAt` by the store's own calendar day; `publishDuePosts` (`studio.publish`, idempotent, "safe to run twice" like `runEmailSends`) is the explicit "send what's due" step a person (or later a worker) presses; every path that can actually publish now also checks the account's own `dailyLimit` (PR 437) and, for Instagram, the platform's own ~50/day ceiling (`PLATFORM_DAILY_CAP`, a platform fact not a business number, CN-018). `SocialPost` gains `scheduledAt`/`approvalRequestId` (already in the S00 skeleton); a `PENDING_APPROVAL` post gets its own `AiApprovalRequest` row (the shared S15 AI 360 table, `growth-agent.ts`'s pattern) so a future central queue page can list it. Admin page gains approve/reject and reschedule controls on each post, a calendar section, an auto-schedule-rules section (add/switch/archive, weekday checkboxes) and a "run due posts now" button; `postPermission` adds `studio.approve`/`studio.publish` routing. 3 pure + 3 real-PostgreSQL package tests for the rule CRUD, 6 new real-PostgreSQL studio-package tests for the queue/calendar/limit, 2 new web `.db.test.ts` cases (rule add/switch/archive; hold → approve → reschedule → calendar → `schedule.runDue`, twice, through the page's own API)

prs.title: Comment and DM ingestion from Facebook, Instagram and TikTok into the Support Inbox (V1 C5.5)
prs.appendixTitle: Comment and DM ingestion from Facebook, Instagram and TikTok into the Support Inbox (V1 C5.5) (derived)

status.note: comment and DM ingestion from Facebook and Instagram into the Support inbox (Blueprint C5.5 point 5, C10 item 6: Doot's community agent "reads comments and DMs … and routes them into the Support Inbox"; no migration — `SupportChannel.kind`/`Integration.provider` are free strings, and `instagram` was already reserved in `channels.ts`): new `@extas/adapters/social-engagement` (Facebook's `feed` webhook field for a Page's own public comments, and Instagram's own `comments`/`messages` fields, each signed the same X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC as Messenger/WhatsApp; two new Keys & connections rows, `facebookPageComments` and `instagramEngagement`, kind `META`, each the mock until its Page/app secret passes the Test); `@extas/support/social-engagement.ts`'s `receiveSocialEngagement` (the webhook's own `receiveMessage` caller, PR 425's pattern) routes a Facebook comment into the SAME `messenger`-kind channel as that Page's Messenger DMs (one Page, one app, two webhook fields) and an Instagram comment or Direct message into the Support core's own `instagram` kind, marking every public comment's words with a fixed `(public comment)` prefix so the team never mistakes a reply typed from the conversation for a private one. Two new webhook routes, `/api/social-comments/facebook` and `/api/social-comments/instagram` (GET handshake, signed POST), mirroring `/api/messenger/webhook`'s own shape. `connectors.ts`'s channel-add validator gains `instagram` (`ADDABLE_CHANNEL_KINDS`); the Support settings page's "Add a channel" kind list gains Instagram. Honest scope, two gaps kept visible rather than faked: (1) no outbound sender is added for either kind — a reply typed from a Facebook-comment or Instagram conversation stays `NOT_SENT · CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`, channels.ts's own existing fallback, until a real sending adapter is built; (2) TikTok comment ingestion is **not built** — TikTok's public API has no webhook that hands a third-party app a video's inbound comments (unlike Facebook's and Instagram's own `feed`/`comments` fields), so no row, no switch and no silently-dead code stands in for it; the register and Blueprint keep "and TikTok" in their words for when that API opens. 4 new adapter-package tests (the two parsers, the Page's/account's own echo left out, the catalogue rows, `exclusive: false` so Studio's own Meta connections are never disabled by this kind) + 3 new support-package real-PostgreSQL tests (only a channel added and switched on takes a message, Facebook comments and DMs share one channel correctly marked, Instagram's own channel, duplicates, switched off) + 2 new web `.db.test.ts` cases (both webhook routes' handshake/signature/routing, through the real connection layer)

status.note: asset model, role taxonomy, immutable originals, generated kept separate (S24 reopened, CN-039/CN-044 AI-2 lane; Blueprint C7.5 step 1, C7.6, V1 C7.22 item 1): new `@extas/photoshoot` package on the `MediaAsset.role`/`isOriginal`/`isAiGenerated`/`sourceAssetId` columns the S00 schema skeleton already carries (no migration). `roles.ts`: the fixed C7.6 taxonomy (`primary_garment`, `front_reference`, `side_reference`, `back_reference`, `detail_reference`, `context_reference`) and `hasBackReference` — the hard rule that a back view is never generated without a real, non-archived `back_reference` on file. `assets.ts`: `tagReferenceRole` (`photoshoot.write`) is the one allowed update to an existing original — only its `role` column, never its file/original fields; `recordGeneratedAsset` (`photoshoot.generate`) always creates a **new** row (`isOriginal: false`, `isAiGenerated: true`, `sourceAssetId` pointing at a real, verified original in the same store — refusing a missing source, one from another store, or one that is itself generated, so an AI image can never trace back to another AI image); `assertNoProtectedFieldChange` guards any future patch endpoint (PR 457's editor) against touching `isOriginal`/`sourceAssetId`/`isAiGenerated`/`storageKey`/`checksumSha256`. prs.title: Provider adapter — part 2 (estimate, generate, status, fetch) (V1 C7.22 item 7)
prs.appendixTitle: Provider adapter — part 2 (estimate, generate, status, fetch) (V1 C7.22 item 7) (derived)

status.note: provider adapter, part 2: estimate/generate/status/fetch (S24 reopened, CN-039; Blueprint C7.5 step 7, C7.6 "cost shown before a batch", C7.19's "headline metric: cost per approved image"; registry v289 `registry-photoshoot-cost.ts`, `studio.photoshoot.rates` — paisa per approved image per provider and tier, 0/not set by default, CN-018; FIX lane: bumped from this branch's own v288 to v289, since PR 447's unrelated `registry-photoshoot.ts` landed first at v288): `PhotoshootProviderApi` (`contract.ts`) grows four methods every provider now answers — `estimate` (pure arithmetic on the owner's own rate, `null` when it is still 0, never an invented cost), `generate` (submits one try-on or ghost-mannequin job), `status` (polls, normalised to `queued`/`processing`/`succeeded`/`failed`, never downloads the output) and `fetch` (reads back a succeeded job's output URLs once, for the caller to download and re-store at once). FASHN: `POST /v1/run` with `{model_name, inputs: {model_image, garment_image, category, seed, num_samples}}`, `GET /v1/status/{id}` mapping its five real status strings, a completed job's spend from the `x-fashn-credits-used` response header (never invented when absent). Fitroom: `POST /api/tryon/v2/tasks` as **multipart form data** — the adapter itself fetches the garment/model image bytes before building the form, since Fitroom takes files, not URLs — `cloth_type` from an explicit top/bottom/one_piece category (Fitroom has no "auto"), `GET /api/tryon/v2/tasks/:id` for status/progress and the temporary `download_signed_url` once `COMPLETED`. Both providers' and the practice provider's `generate` refuse up front (no network call) when the job kind is outside the connected provider's own capabilities (`requirePhotoshootJobSupported`) or a required image is missing — the C7.6 "never invent a back view" spirit applied one level down, to the job call itself. The mock encodes its whole round trip in the job id itself (no database here) and, honestly, hands back the garment shot as its own "output" rather than fabricating one (the PR 439/440 rule). 26 new tests (`photoshoot-provider.test.ts`, now 41), a new settings test (`registry-photoshoot-cost.test.ts`) and its English/Bengali labels (`messages/photoshoot-cost.{en,bn}.json`) — all against stand-in servers, never the real network or a real key. No new admin page; no job orchestration yet (queue, retries, idempotency) — that is PR 451–452.

Marketing › Studio › Videos: each job row gets its own next-move button — "Queue it" on a waiting clip, "Run it" on a queued one, "Retry" (with its attempt count) on a failed one up to the cap — each move re-reads the page. status.note: image-to-video engine — part 3, best-of-2 and review/approve (S25, CN-039; Blueprint C8.2; registry v289 `studio.video` adds `bestOfTwo`, off — CN-018 off-by-default perk; v288 was taken by PR 447's registry-photoshoot.ts, merged first; no migration): `@extas/adapters`'s video contract gains an optional `passes` on `VideoEstimateInput` (`estimateFromRate` multiplies by it, default 1) and an optional `score` on `VideoClipResult` (the mock never sets one); `@extas/creative-studio`'s `video.ts` gains `BEST_OF_PASSES` (2, a technical constant, not CN-018's business number) and reads `studio.video.bestOfTwo` in `estimateVideoJob`/`requestVideoJob` (the quote is already doubled, never a surprise after the fact) and in `runVideoJob`, which now runs `BEST_OF_PASSES` passes — always, not only as a retry-on-failure — and keeps the `SUCCEEDED` pass with the higher `score` (ties, and every pass against the mock, keep the first that succeeded); `actualMinor` bills the single-pass rate × the passes actually run either way. `approveVideoJob`/`rejectVideoJob` move a `REVIEW_REQUIRED` job to `APPROVED`/`REJECTED`, `WRONG_STATE` from anywhere else; `VideoJobView` gains `providerJobId`/`actualMinor` (a pre-existing gap — PR 482/483 stored them but never surfaced them). prs.title: Reel assembly — part 2 (V1 C8.6 item 6)
prs.appendixTitle: Reel assembly — part 2 (V1 C8.6 item 6) (derived)

status.note: reel assembly — part 2, the actual compositor (S25, CN-039; Blueprint C8.1, C8.6 item 6; no registry change, no migration): `@extas/creative-studio`'s `reel.ts` gains `assembleReel`, which moves a `DRAFT` (or previously `FAILED`) reel's status to `ASSEMBLED` and fills `Reel.outputAssetIds` — one per chosen aspect. No real video encoder exists yet (the same honest gap PR 439/482 set), so nothing is actually stitched, mixed or baked in: the output is the **first named clip's own already-approved real output asset** (`VideoJob.outputAssetId`), reused for every chosen shape — a real, already-existing file, never fabricated footage or a pretend per-shape crop; falls back to the next clip in order when an earlier one has no output yet. Re-checks every clip is still of this store and still `APPROVED` (`NOT_FOUND`/`CLIPS_NOT_READY`, the same codes `buildReel` uses — a clip's review can never be assumed still good) and, when music was chosen, that it is still a real audio asset of this store (`NOT_FOUND`/`SOURCE_INVALID`); refuses a set-aside reel (`WRONG_STATE` — bring it back first) or one already `ASSEMBLED` (`WRONG_STATE` — never redone silently); lands `FAILED` (never throws) when none of the clips has a usable output yet, and a `FAILED` reel may be tried again once one does, with no attempt cap (this reads data only, it never calls a provider or spends money, unlike `retryVideoJob`'s capped retries). Marketing › Studio › Reels: a `DRAFT` or `FAILED` row gets an "Assemble this reel" button; once `ASSEMBLED` the row shows a note that the output is a preview, not a real stitched video. `marketing.studio.write`; admin guide and both message files updated. 9 new `.db.test.ts` cases (real PostgreSQL, skip-safe without `TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL`): assembling fills one output per shape from the first clip's own real output, falls back to the next clip when the first has none, lands `FAILED` with no usable output, a `FAILED` reel can be tried again once a clip has one, refuses a second assembly of an already-`ASSEMBLED` reel, refuses an archived reel, refuses a clip that stopped being `APPROVED` since drafting, refuses a music track that stopped being valid since drafting, refuses an unknown reel id.

prs.appendixTitle: Campaign creative export — part 1 (V1 C8.6 item 7) (derived)

status.note: campaign creative export — part 1 (S25, CN-039; Blueprint C8.1, C8.5, C8.6 item 7; no registry change, no migration — the `CreativeExport` model was already in the full S00 schema, additive, unused until now): new `@extas/creative-studio`'s `export.ts` — `requestCreativeExport` from a campaign picks exactly one of a product, a SKU or a category (Blueprint C8.5's own three choices; `SELECTION_EMPTY` names none, `INVALID_INPUT` names more than one), checks it is a real, non-archived record of this store (`NOT_FOUND`) that already has at least one real, non-archived `ProductMedia` to export from — a SKU counts its product's shared media plus its own colour's; a category counts any of its products' (`SOURCE_INVALID` otherwise — nothing to export from an empty product); an optional campaign or creative brief, when named, must be a real record of this store too (`NOT_FOUND`). `CREATIVE_EXPORT_SIZES` (Blueprint C8.5: Meta 1:1/4:5/9:16, Google 1.91:1, TikTok 9:16 — five technical format keys, not a CN-018 number) picks the platform sizes; `withOverlay` and `landingUrl` are carried through for PR 488. prs.appendixTitle: Provider adapter — part 2 (estimate, generate, status, fetch) (V1 C7.22 item 7) (derived)

status.note: provider adapter, part 2: estimate/generate/status/fetch (S24 reopened, CN-039; Blueprint C7.5 step 7, C7.6 "cost shown before a batch", C7.19's "headline metric: cost per approved image"; registry v289 `registry-photoshoot-cost.ts`, `studio.photoshoot.rates` — paisa per approved image per provider and tier, 0/not set by default, CN-018; FIX lane: bumped from this branch's own v288 to v289, since PR 447's unrelated `registry-photoshoot.ts` landed first at v288): `PhotoshootProviderApi` (`contract.ts`) grows four methods every provider now answers — `estimate` (pure arithmetic on the owner's own rate, `null` when it is still 0, never an invented cost), `generate` (submits one try-on or ghost-mannequin job), `status` (polls, normalised to `queued`/`processing`/`succeeded`/`failed`, never downloads the output) and `fetch` (reads back a succeeded job's output URLs once, for the caller to download and re-store at once). FASHN: `POST /v1/run` with `{model_name, inputs: {model_image, garment_image, category, seed, num_samples}}`, `GET /v1/status/{id}` mapping its five real status strings, a completed job's spend from the `x-fashn-credits-used` response header (never invented when absent). Fitroom: `POST /api/tryon/v2/tasks` as **multipart form data** — the adapter itself fetches the garment/model image bytes before building the form, since Fitroom takes files, not URLs — `cloth_type` from an explicit top/bottom/one_piece category (Fitroom has no "auto"), `GET /api/tryon/v2/tasks/:id` for status/progress and the temporary `download_signed_url` once `COMPLETED`. Both providers' and the practice provider's `generate` refuse up front (no network call) when the job kind is outside the connected provider's own capabilities (`requirePhotoshootJobSupported`) or a required image is missing — the C7.6 "never invent a back view" spirit applied one level down, to the job call itself. The mock encodes its whole round trip in the job id itself (no database here) and, honestly, hands back the garment shot as its own "output" rather than fabricating one (the PR 439/440 rule). 26 new tests (`photoshoot-provider.test.ts`, now 41), a new settings test (`registry-photoshoot-cost.test.ts`) and its English/Bengali labels (`messages/photoshoot-cost.{en,bn}.json`) — all against stand-in servers, never the real network or a real key. No new admin page; no job orchestration yet (queue, retries, idempotency) — that is PR 451–452.

status.note: image-to-video engine — part 3, best-of-2 and review/approve (S25, CN-039; Blueprint C8.2; registry v289 `studio.video` adds `bestOfTwo`, off — CN-018 off-by-default perk; v288 was taken by PR 447's registry-photoshoot.ts, merged first; no migration): `@extas/adapters`'s video contract gains an optional `passes` on `VideoEstimateInput` (`estimateFromRate` multiplies by it, default 1) and an optional `score` on `VideoClipResult` (the mock never sets one); `@extas/creative-studio`'s `video.ts` gains `BEST_OF_PASSES` (2, a technical constant, not CN-018's business number) and reads `studio.video.bestOfTwo` in `estimateVideoJob`/`requestVideoJob` (the quote is already doubled, never a surprise after the fact) and in `runVideoJob`, which now runs `BEST_OF_PASSES` passes — always, not only as a retry-on-failure — and keeps the `SUCCEEDED` pass with the higher `score` (ties, and every pass against the mock, keep the first that succeeded); `actualMinor` bills the single-pass rate × the passes actually run either way. `approveVideoJob`/`rejectVideoJob` move a `REVIEW_REQUIRED` job to `APPROVED`/`REJECTED`, `WRONG_STATE` from anywhere else; `VideoJobView` gains `providerJobId`/`actualMinor` (a pre-existing gap — PR 482/483 stored them but never surfaced them). prs.appendixTitle: Reel assembly — part 2 (V1 C8.6 item 6) (derived)

status.note: reel assembly — part 2, the actual compositor (S25, CN-039; Blueprint C8.1, C8.6 item 6; no registry change, no migration): `@extas/creative-studio`'s `reel.ts` gains `assembleReel`, which moves a `DRAFT` (or previously `FAILED`) reel's status to `ASSEMBLED` and fills `Reel.outputAssetIds` — one per chosen aspect. No real video encoder exists yet (the same honest gap PR 439/482 set), so nothing is actually stitched, mixed or baked in: the output is the **first named clip's own already-approved real output asset** (`VideoJob.outputAssetId`), reused for every chosen shape — a real, already-existing file, never fabricated footage or a pretend per-shape crop; falls back to the next clip in order when an earlier one has no output yet. Re-checks every clip is still of this store and still `APPROVED` (`NOT_FOUND`/`CLIPS_NOT_READY`, the same codes `buildReel` uses — a clip's review can never be assumed still good) and, when music was chosen, that it is still a real audio asset of this store (`NOT_FOUND`/`SOURCE_INVALID`); refuses a set-aside reel (`WRONG_STATE` — bring it back first) or one already `ASSEMBLED` (`WRONG_STATE` — never redone silently); lands `FAILED` (never throws) when none of the clips has a usable output yet, and a `FAILED` reel may be tried again once one does, with no attempt cap (this reads data only, it never calls a provider or spends money, unlike `retryVideoJob`'s capped retries). Marketing › Studio › Reels: a `DRAFT` or `FAILED` row gets an "Assemble this reel" button; once `ASSEMBLED` the row shows a note that the output is a preview, not a real stitched video. `marketing.studio.write`; admin guide and both message files updated. 9 new `.db.test.ts` cases (real PostgreSQL, skip-safe without `TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL`): assembling fills one output per shape from the first clip's own real output, falls back to the next clip when the first has none, lands `FAILED` with no usable output, a `FAILED` reel can be tried again once a clip has one, refuses a second assembly of an already-`ASSEMBLED` reel, refuses an archived reel, refuses a clip that stopped being `APPROVED` since drafting, refuses a music track that stopped being valid since drafting, refuses an unknown reel id.
